correctness.rationale: In a tournament an acyclic/transitive vertex set has a source. In the cyclic block, that source forces all other vertices into one interval of length \(m+1\), while any subset of such an interval is transitive; hence its flag complex is the cyclic nerve \(N(n,m)\), homotopy equivalent to \(S^1\) for \(1\le m<n/2\) by the primary circular-arc nerve classification. No transitive face intersects all three blocks, so the full complex is the cyclic union of the three pairwise joins. Its two-stage homotopy pushout has three join summands, three suspensions and one extra \(S^1\) from the two-component final intersection. Thus the claimed wedge follows with \(X*X\simeq S^3\) and \(\Sigma X\simeq S^2\). The actual verify.py enumerates transitive faces and boundary ranks for \(n=3,5\), gives \(n=5\) face vector \((15,105,315,450,300,75)\) and Betti vector \((1,1,3,3,0,0)\); this agrees with, but does not replace, the proof. Each vertex has outdegree \(m+n=(3n-1)/2\); common out-neighbor counts vary, excluding double regularity.

final_claim: For every odd \(n=2m+1\ge3\), let \(R_n\) be the cyclic regular tournament, and replace each vertex of a directed 3-cycle with \(R_n\). The resulting regular but not doubly regular tournament \(T_n\) has directed flag complex \(\operatorname{dFl}(T_n)\simeq S^1\vee\bigvee^3S^2\vee\bigvee^3S^3\).
limitations: The assertion is for the specified three-block lexicographic tournament with odd block size; it does not classify all regular tournaments or equivariant/simple homotopy types.
The finite verifier checks the first two block sizes only; the proof of the universal statement uses the cyclic-nerve theorem and homotopy pushouts.
